# TradingView-API
# https://github.com/Mathieu2301/TradingView-API
# https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mathieuc/tradingview

Independent community library for TradingView market data. Not an official TradingView API.
Version 4 is the default npm release: TypeScript, ESM, Node >= 20 or Bun. Breaking rewrite of v3 (no compatibility layer). Install with npm install @mathieuc/tradingview. Existing V3 projects should consult docs/migration-v4.md before upgrading.

Simple data API (import from '@mathieuc/tradingview/data' or the root entry):
- getCandles({ symbol, timeframe?, count?, from?, to?, chartType?, ... }) -> Candle[] oldest first, time in Unix seconds.
- watchCandles(query, { onData, onError? }) -> watcher { latest, stop(), closed }.
- getQuote(symbol), getQuotes({ symbols }), watchQuotes({ symbols }, { onData }).
- getSymbolInfo(symbol), getIndicatorData({ symbol, indicator, inputs? }), watchIndicator(...).
- getScreener({ columns, market?, filter?, sort?, range?, symbols? }) -> { totalCount, rows }; one HTTP page, not a streaming screener.
- getHotlist({ kind, ... }) -> scanner-ranked rows, not guaranteed TradingView UI parity.
- getWatchlists({ credentials }) -> read-only account lists with ordered symbols and section markers.
- searchMarkets(text), searchIndicators(text), getTechnicalAnalysis(symbol).
- Websocket data calls accept timeoutMs, signal (AbortSignal), credentials ({ session, signature }) and client (shared TradingViewClient). HTTP lookups accept signal in options.
- Candle calls can use a custom MarketDataProvider; TradingViewProvider is the default source adapter.
- Errors are TradingViewError with a code (SYMBOL_ERROR, TIMEOUT, STUDY_ERROR, NO_DATA...).

Low-level API: TradingViewClient, client.createChart() (ChartSession: setMarket, setTimeframe, fetchMore, replay, createStudy), client.createQuoteSession(), PineIndicator, BuiltInIndicator, HTTP functions (loginUser, getUser, getIndicator, getPrivateIndicators, getDrawings, PinePermissionManager).

Pine studies need a TradingView account (session cookies). Built-in studies and candles/quotes work anonymously, with history limits.
Docs: docs/data-api.md, docs/backtest.md, docs/low-level-api.md, docs/migration-v4.md, docs/v4-coverage.md, docs/v4-reliability.md, docs/protocol-contributing.md. Examples: examples/.
Backtest API (import from '@mathieuc/tradingview/backtest'; since 4.1.0-beta.1, npm tag beta): write only the entry rule, do not write an engine.
- backtest({ symbol, timeframe, years?, credentials?, signal, exits?, fee?, slippage?, splitRatio?, runs?, seed? }) -> { report, snapshot }. runBacktest(candles | snapshot, options) -> report, synchronous, no network.
- signal(candles) -> [{ bar, direction: 'long' | 'short', refs? }]: decided at the close of `bar` using bars 0..bar only; entry is always the next bar's open. Optional signal.warmupBars (default 200) and signal.label.
- The engine reruns signal on truncated history and throws TradingViewError code LOOK_AHEAD if a signal depends on later bars (or repaints).
- Built in: rsiDivergence(options), defaultExits() (fixed_1.5R, fixed_2R, atr1.5_2R, trail_atr3), fixedExit, atrExit, atrTrailingExit, indicators sma/ema/rsi/atr/findPivots.
- Protocol: frozen snapshot with SHA-256 (loadSnapshot to replay), warm-up never traded, 70/30 IS/OOS split with no position across it, fee 0.1% + slippage 0.05% per side, same-candle stop+target = loss, gap = open, 1000 seeded random-entry runs per exit and split with percentile and p5/p50/p95.
- report is plain JSON: snapshot info, segments with dates, signals, rows (metrics: trades, netReturn, winRate, profitFactor or null, maxDrawdown; baseline; percentile), trades with bar indices and times, causality, warnings. formatReport(report), tradesToCsv(report.trades).
- No claim of profitability: a negative or inconclusive result is a valid outcome. Docs: docs/backtest.md. Example: examples/honest-backtest/.
The interactive setup CLI is available with npx @mathieuc/tradingview. It opens Molted Studio, launches a local coding agent with a prompt, prints that prompt, or installs the library. It is not a market-data query CLI. No MCP server or hosted trading API is shipped, and the library places no orders.
Questions and bugs: https://github.com/Mathieu2301/TradingView-API/issues/new/choose
